title.en: Let the mechanism change the geometry that causes it

summary: When a scene explains a mechanism, animate the geometric quantity that does the work, not a colour or a proxy.
objective: Make mechanistic animations show the actual structural change that the explanation depends on.
applies_when: A scene explains how a structure produces force, motion or binding.
A slider or playback controls the degree of contraction, binding or engagement.
A quantity such as force or output is displayed alongside the structure.
intent_signals: why does force change with length
example_prompts: Show a sarcomere contracting with the bands changing correctly.
Explain why force depends on how much the filaments overlap.
negative_signals: Decorative pulsing or glow effects used to suggest activity.
Whole-body motion where the internal mechanism is not the subject.
not_for: Decorative pulsing or glow effects used to suggest activity.
Whole-body motion where the internal mechanism is not the subject.

principles: An explanation lives in the changing geometry. If the animation shortens a whole block or brightens a colour, the viewer learns that something happened, not how.

In the sliding filament model the filaments do not change length; the thin filaments slide past the thick ones, the Z lines approach, the I band narrows and the A band keeps its width. That specific pattern is the content.

Structural sourcing does not supply a force model. Constant filament lengths and moving band boundaries are supported structure; a force readout needs its own sourced relationship, with stated activation and operating assumptions. Either show force from a separately sourced length-tension curve, correctly parameterised to the same sarcomere length, or show no force at all.
Getting the invariant wrong is a visible error: filaments that shorten teach exactly the misconception the model exists to correct.
implementation: Model the components whose relative positions carry the mechanism, and drive them from one parameter such as sarcomere length.
Keep the invariant explicit in the construction: fixed filament lengths with variable overlap, rather than scaled meshes.
Derive the displayed bands, zones or measurements from the same geometry so they cannot drift.
Include the range where the mechanism degrades, such as too little or excessive overlap, since the ends of the range are where the explanation is tested.

Where force appears, label its origin and its assumptions: a reproduced length-tension curve from a cited source, or a model whose parameters are stated. A sourced measurement curve is not wrong merely because it is not recomputed from the displayed mesh overlap; what must agree is the sarcomere-length parameter used by both.
observable_checks: Measure the modelled filament lengths across the range; any change means the geometry contradicts the mechanism.
Check the band widths at several lengths: the A band should keep its width while the I band narrows.

If a force readout is shown, confirm it is driven by the same sarcomere-length parameter as the geometry and that its source or model is named; a structural view with no force claim passes this check by showing nothing.
Push the parameter to its extremes and confirm the model behaves sensibly instead of inverting.

creative_affordances: Schematic proportions, exaggerated spacing and colour coding all help; the invariant is the constancy of filament length, not visual realism.
An accompanying abstract diagram of overlap against force is a legitimate companion view.
known_limits: Authored mechanism guidance citing one structural model; it does not assert numerical force values or molecular kinetics.
Cross-bridge cycling detail and calcium regulation are outside this rule.

claims.statement: In the sliding filament model of contraction the thin filaments are pulled past the thick filaments without the filaments themselves changing length, so that the Z lines move closer together and the I band becomes smaller while the A band keeps the same width.
claims.scope: Structural description of skeletal muscle contraction at the sarcomere level; it does not describe force magnitudes or molecular kinetics.

source_refs.locator: 10.3, The Sliding Filament Model of Contraction
